title: [AUG-75] RCA: Groq purple color scheme missed during FE audit
why_we_need_this: During AUG-71 Major FE Audit, the agent audited the semantic color pass across all components but excluded the Groq integration's purple color scheme (#7c5cbf light / #a88de0 dark) from the violation list. The SAVE button, link color, and input focus border all use purple — a color entirely outside the brandbook Necron palette. The agent rationalized this as "intentional third-party branding" without flagging it for user decision, violating the audit's mandate to check EVERY element against brandbook rules. Three prior RCA tasks (AUG-73 for skipping color pass entirely, AUG-74 for missing semantic title classification) indicate a pattern of incomplete audit coverage that self-justifies exclusions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Root cause documented: agent applied subjective "brand exception" reasoning to exclude Groq purple from violation list without user approval — the brandbook has no exception clause for third-party colors
2. Add rule to agent constraints: during brandbook audits, NEVER self-exempt elements based on assumed design intent — flag ALL deviations and let the user decide which are intentional exceptions
3. Add rule: when an agent's output does not match the scope/expectations of the initial task, an RCA task MUST be created automatically before proceeding — this is a mandatory process gate, not optional
4. Update @project-context/frontend-design/README.md audit rules to explicitly state: third-party integration components (Groq, Praxis, etc.) are NOT exempt from the brandbook — all UI within the product follows the same color system
5. All rules documented in project context and agent memory
